head.2: AIDE is a desktop code editor with an AI studio inside: an agent, a design canvas and a team of 12 roles in one window. Tauri 2, Rust, React. Your keys stay with you.
head.3: A code editor with a whole AI studio inside: an agent, design, and a team with faces.

doc-agent.1: [b]Permissions.[/b] Writing files and running terminal commands happen only after you click “Allow”.
doc-agent.2: [b]Report.[/b] Each reply ends with a list of actions, e.g. “Done: 6 actions ›”, and the number of tokens spent.
doc-agent.3: [b]Undo.[/b] A checkpoint is created before any edit. The “Undo” button restores the changed files.
doc-agent.4: [b]Stop.[/b] Cuts the request to the model instantly.
doc-agent.5: [b]Edit a selection.[/b] Select code and press [kbd]Ctrl[/kbd]+[kbd]K[/kbd]: the changes appear as a diff you can accept or reject.
doc-crew.1: Twelve roles with faces, voices and skills: team lead, design, front, back, QA, DevOps, analyst, lawyer, accountant, marketer, intern and joker. You're the CEO: you set the task, the roles discuss it and split the work.
doc-crew.2: Only roles with “hands” can change files and run commands — the rest advise and review. Role actions go through the same permissions as the agent's.
doc-keys.10: Have the agent edit the selected code
doc-keys.11: Close the palette, settings or edit
doc-modes.1: The switch in the window header changes the whole interface. The project, the history and the agent stay the same.
doc-modes.2: An editor on CodeMirror 6, file tree, tabbed terminals, Git and search. The agent lives in the chat on the right.
doc-modes.3: Describe the result in words. The team lead splits the task into steps, the roles do them, QA checks.
doc-modes.4: Build a mockup on the canvas, then press “Create in project” and pick a stack: HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js or Astro.
doc-rules.1: Put [code]AGENTS.md[/code] or [code]CLAUDE.md[/code] in the project root — the agent reads these rules before it starts.
doc-rules.2: Your own chat commands: create a file [code].aide/commands/name.md[/code] with the prompt. It shows up in chat as [code]/name[/code], and [code]$ARGUMENTS[/code] is replaced with whatever you type after the command.
doc-start.1: Install [code]Node.js 20+[/code], [code]Rust[/code] and the Tauri 2 prerequisites for Windows.
doc-start.2: In the project folder run [code]npm install[/code], then [code]npm run tauri dev[/code].
doc-start.4: Connect a model in the settings. The API key is stored in the Windows credential store, not in files.
